findings.text: The route definition added for contour_min_wall_distance_m (minimum distance from the traced axis-enclosing contour to the published wall contact) is global, but the before rows under the same key (:22 0.2720145779546779, :37 0.20974874944500732) were produced under an earlier meaning and do not reproduce under the new one - measured 0.8735099516 m from the before contact to its own contour at its own level. A reader comparing the landing record's control gap 0.012811640 m with the receipt's before-row 0.2720145779546779 is comparing two different quantities filed under one key.

The after panel draws the boundary level through draw_flux_contours in separatrix style over the whole level set, and at the after level 0.25673503858584695 that set carries three closed components (measured from the fixture: lower-divertor lobe R 0.4598-0.5856, Z -1.80 to -1.63; the in-vessel axis-enclosing component R 0.1953-1.0505; upper-divertor lobe R 0.4534-0.6028, Z 1.6166-1.8190). The detached upper-divertor lobe is therefore drawn in the boundary style with nothing marking it as not the boundary, on the one figure whose purpose is to show the contact moving off a detached lobe; it should be shown with a distinguishing mark (hollow or dashed) or the caption should state the component count and which one is the boundary.

containment_required is computed once from the pre-containment provisional pass and reused by both containment passes (:1155, :1177). On this fixture a class-free read (requested_class=None) resolves it False, so the wall anchor stays the detached contact at 0.25850360061597305 while the read still ends classified diverted (measured: diverted True, wall_point [0.599080815463746, 1.7280815839767456]). That is self-consistent - a diverted read publishes the X-point as its boundary - but the containment contract is exercised only for class-pinned limited reads, and no test asserts the class-free path keeps an axis-connected anchor.

The record cites the gate as the three topology test files at 33 passed. The 33 is real and re-run first-hand in one all_debug CPU job (33 passed in 323.42 s), but it spans four files: tests/test_jax_topology.py 11 + tests/test_limited_boundary_touches_wall.py 7 + tests/test_topology_limiter_contact.py 9 + tests/test_limiter_topology_receipts.py 6. The three named files alone give 27 passed in 249.99 s. A later reader re-running the three named files gets 27 and should not read the difference as a regression.

justifications.durability: The replaced assertion is a real guard, not a tautology: the traversed reference is an independent scipy RectBivariateSpline plus _trace_surfaces trace, and the discriminating pair was measured first-hand (containment on -> :184 passes at 0.001252 m; containment off -> 0.873160 m > pitch -> fails). tests/test_jax_topology.py:610 now requires zero vertical-half-plane label differences and the docstring records the historical 51 as the disagreement before the spline-authored contact, so the historical reading survives as prose instead of an equality nobody can re-derive. Deductions: the admission rule has no unit-level pin of its own - the only place a non-axis component is refused is this one persisted fixture, so a regression that admits a detached contact on a different raster would pass every test here; and the bounds sit two orders above the measured margins (1.25 mm against a 125 mm pitch), so the guard speaks only after the defect is large.
justifications.evidence: Every quantitative claim reproduced from docs/figures/null-identification-authority/limited-touch/row-16-terminal-state.npz with no new solve. Contact (0.19524440169334412, -0.011792924701615214) equals the receipt to 0.0 m; contact flux 0.25673503858584695 equals the receipt; an independent RectBivariateSpline evaluated at the contact gives 0.25673503858584656 (|diff| 3.886e-16 against the receipt's 1.51e-15 relative claim). The traced axis-enclosing contour passes 0.0012517198875053154 m from the contact (receipt identical; the 1.25 mm claim) and its global wall approach is 3.062084605542914e-06 m (receipt identical). The old contact (0.6050537429416492, 1.7280815839767456) measures 0.8928708266280256 m from the axis-enclosing contour at its own level - the 0.893 m claim - and that contour's unrelated wall approach is 0.012811640333972418 m, matching the landing record's 0.012811640 m. Axis enclosure verified independently by ray casting with matplotlib Path on the closed trace. The guard was shown to refuse and not merely to pass: with containment disabled the read publishes the detached contact 0.873160 m away and tests/test_limited_boundary_touches_wall.py:184 fails against pitch 0.125 m. Deductions recorded as FINDING 1 and FINDING 4.
justifications.fit: The change consumes the existing axis_component flood and the existing contour spline instead of adding a new detector, and it keeps the article's one-boundary-authority invariant: the published contract is the contour's own level, evaluated on the same spline the contour is traced from. Deduction: the screen runs one component flood per wall node per structured read inside a vmap, and the record reports no compile or wall cost for the new read, while compile cost is a declared lead priority (a 12-arm sweep at 7551 s); the per-read cost should be measured before the labeller repeats it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Implemented as the article writes it: nova/equilibrium/topology.py:492 builds a fixed-shape bracket table over every wall node and vmaps the quadratic fit, and :583 admits a contact only when the axis-connected component at that contact's own spline level reaches it within one lattice pitch. Containment is decided inside the traced program by the same vmap the production flood uses (psi_mask -> axis_component -> label_saddle_aware_hex_connected_components, n_iter = confined.size as a static arg), so the program is fixed-shape with no data-dependent control flow and the empty-eligible case is guarded by jnp.any at :558. Row 17 is not regenerated and the receipt says so (measurement_status "not-regenerated") rather than claiming a metric. Deduction recorded as FINDING 3: the containment contract is reachable only when the class is pinned to LIMITED.
justifications.scope_discipline: The two non-merge commits touch only nova/equilibrium/topology.py, tests/test_jax_topology.py, tests/test_limited_boundary_touches_wall.py, docs/figures/null-identification-authority/limited-touch/{receipt.json,row-16-before-after.svg} and the plan's own landing comment; the plan edit is confined to the follow-up article and its comment. No shared-environment mutation (no uv sync in any command), no index, sprint or unrelated plan write. Both non-merge commits carry a body, and all three commits (including the merge fe0689ce) are clean of attribution on the line-anchored check.
